{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nm-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"28cf3ce2e5e47c42c73e69cb7db08657cf3a6e1506644dcacc6659806c1eade5","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nm-class-std:lineage:54","source_registry_sha256":"22599efcb4852b796972acef6eb09f4cfe8d16ca15887f7ea7660c7748b4df92","source_liveness_sha256":"6766993f61347d495f390e08c7d8b1c44de597b6249cdb10686ea7f9f38e1ea3"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Space cushions, merging and safe passing","heading":"C — Space cushions, merging and safe passing","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Space cushions, merging and safe passing

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
More separation from other road users gives you additional time to respond. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Following too close can cause a rear-end collision when the leading vehicle stops suddenly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
For the three-second following check, note when the leading vehicle’s rear passes a fixed roadside marker, then count until you reach that marker. [A02] [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A02
If you reach the following-distance marker before completing three seconds, you are too close. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A02
Increase the gap and repeat the following-distance check until at least three seconds separate you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A02
The manual gives a four-second following gap as a potentially needed increase on slippery roads or behind a motorcycle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A02
A heavy load or trailer, or following an emergency vehicle, can require a four-second following gap in the manual’s examples. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A02
The handbook also lists approaching railroad crossings and being stopped on a hill or incline as situations that may need four seconds of following space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A02
Maintain steady speed and signal slowing or turning early to help a following driver keep a safe gap. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A02
Keep space on each side so you have room to turn or change lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
On a road with at least two lanes, make room for vehicles entering. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
Allow additional side space beside parked cars. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
Give pedestrians and cyclists extra space, with particular care around children. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
The handbook specifies a gap of about four seconds when merging with traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Entering halfway into a four-second gap leaves roughly two seconds ahead and two seconds behind. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
The handbook applies its four-second merge gap to lane changes, roadway entry and a lane joining another lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Do not force a merge into insufficient space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
When crossing multiple lanes, move across one lane at a time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Crossing traffic requires a gap large enough to clear the entire roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
Entering traffic requires enough room to complete the turn and accelerate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
Before a left turn, verify that neither vehicles nor pedestrians obstruct your path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
A green signal does not justify starting across when vehicles block your route. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
Enter railroad tracks only with sufficient space to clear them without stopping on the rails. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0027]

Misconceptions: a green signal does not create space beyond an obstructed intersection; merge-gap examples do not replace ongoing following-distance checks.
Mnemonics: see the gap, clear the path, cross one lane at a time.
Glossary: a space cushion is separation around the vehicle; a merge gap is room to join traffic.
Dynamic facts: actual traction, traffic gaps, visibility, road markings and crossing conditions require fresh checks.
